correct_completion: the team sent it to the director.
full_sentence: Having finished the report, the team sent it to the director.
acceptable_variants: the team then sent it to the director.
they sent it to the director straight away.

options.text: the report was sent to the director by the team.
options.why_wrong: This is a dangling participle: the report cannot have finished itself, so the subject of the main clause must be the person who finished the report.

options.text: to send it to the director.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive phrase cannot serve as the main clause of the sentence; a finite verb is needed.

options.text: the team sent it to the director.
the director sent it back to the team.
options.why_wrong: The director did not finish the report, so the participle clause does not match the subject of the main clause.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses and the rule that the implied subject must match the main clause subject
explanation: In 'Having finished the report, ...', the implied subject of the participle clause must be the same as the subject of the main clause. Russian speakers often build similar clauses with деепричастия, which follow the same logic, but English is stricter about the subject, so mismatched subjects produce dangling modifiers.
translation: Закончив отчет, команда отправила его директору.
